answers.answer: Select number of players + 1 Factory cards face-down; return the rest unseen. Put one encounter token on each of 11 marked territories, and randomly choose one structure bonus tile face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
answers.evidence: Setup: 'number of players + 1'; '11 marked territories'; 'one structure bonus tile'; 'lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.'

answers.answer: Character starts at home base; two workers go on the two land-adjoined territories adjoining it; four mechs start over the Faction Mat abilities; six stars by the faction emblem; six cubes in the Player Mat green boxes marked black; four structures in matching Player Mat boxes; four recruits in its bottom-row circles; six remaining workers on its Produce red rectangles; action token beside the Player Mat. Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw; Player Mat sets popularity, coins, and two objectives.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3–4 enumerate mat assignments and each starting piece.

answers.answer: You may take the top action, bottom action, both, or neither, but must move the token to a different section from last turn. Bottom-first is prohibited. Rusviet may repeat a section from last turn, but each action remains limited to once that turn. Top-row gains may pay bottom-row cost. Pay all exposed red-box costs in full before the action, then choose any amount of exposed green-box benefits; exact bottom costs and coin benefits vary by Player Mat and upgrades.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: different section, optional top then bottom; full cost then optional benefit; Rusviet limitation.

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls it and its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities; you retain those abilities except an uncontrolled Mill cannot produce. Pay action resources from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: enemy worker control; 'Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities'; pay from any controlled territories.

answers.answer: No: on an unupgraded Move, select up to two different units and move each one adjacent territory; one unit cannot use both selections to move twice. A carried worker may subsequently move itself, and a worker may move onto a mech and be carried by its subsequent move. All units can pick up, carry, and drop any number of resources; only mechs may also carry any number of your workers, never your character.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: 'two different units'; carried worker movement; all-unit resource carrying and mech worker carrying.

answers.answer: The Speed-enabled mech may enter, but stops and cannot move again that turn. Enemy workers immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources; you lose one popularity per worker down to zero, and insufficient popularity does not prevent retreat. Your workers cannot enter independently while enemy workers control that territory.
answers.evidence: Move: enemy workers only; entry stops, workers retreat, popularity loss down to zero; your workers cannot enter independently.

answers.answer: After all units finish a Move action, resolve any combats before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses the order of multiple combats. Your workers cannot independently move into or out of territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.
answers.evidence: Move: finish moving other units, then resolve all combats before bottom action; attacker chooses order; worker restriction.

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gains two power or one combat card before upgrades. If the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck; if both deck and discards are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1 and gains any two resources (same or different) or one popularity, before upgrades. Traded resources go on a controlled territory with at least one worker; if all your workers are at home, you cannot Trade for resources.
answers.evidence: Bolster and Trade sections state costs, choices, placement, all-workers-at-home rule, and deck exhaustion.

answers.answer: First pay all exposed Produce costs in full (power, popularity and/or coins), then choose up to two different controlled territories before upgrades; each worker there may produce one matching terrain token on that territory. New workers come left to right from the Player Mat and are placed in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Exposing new costs affects future Produce actions, not the cost already paid.
answers.evidence: Produce steps 1–3: full payment before production; new workers left to right; production may be declined; new costs affect future actions.

answers.answer: Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens in exposed Upgrade cost boxes on your Player Mat; Deploy costs the number of metal tokens in exposed Deploy cost boxes; both amounts vary by mat and upgrades. Upgrade moves a cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost; solid-black-bordered red boxes cannot be upgraded. Deploy puts a chosen mech on a controlled territory containing your worker, never a lake, and its uncovered ability then applies to your character and all mechs, not workers. Even after completing all such pieces, you may still pay for the bottom action to gain its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: Upgrade, Deploy, and completed-bottom-action paragraphs.

answers.answer: Build on a controlled territory with your worker; one structure total per territory, including opponents' structures; Factory is allowed, lakes and home bases are forbidden. Structures cannot be moved or destroyed. A controlled Mill gives its bonus Produce territory; if enemy units control its territory, the Mill cannot produce, although you retain other structure abilities. Your Mine remains a personal tunnel for your unit movement even when enemy-controlled; opponents cannot use your building abilities.
answers.evidence: Build: placement and permanence; Mill only while controlled; Mine personal tunnel even when enemy-controlled.

answers.answer: Take a recruit from any bottom-row section of your Player Mat and put it permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus on your Faction Mat. Immediately gain the chosen one-time bonus: two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. Its ongoing bonus is the circle uncovered where the recruit was removed. When you, your immediate left, or immediate right neighbor takes that corresponding bottom action, resolve active player first, then left, then right, stopping if a sixth star ends the game. In two-player play the opponent triggers the bonus once, not twice.
answers.evidence: Enlist and Ongoing recruits paragraphs.

answers.answer: Both combatants simultaneously and secretly choose dial power from 0 through the smaller of seven and their current power. They may each add up to one combat card per participating character/mech, including at zero dial power; Rusviet People's Army adds one total card if workers are present. If both combatants have combat mech abilities, attacker uses theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously, add dial and card values, and attacker wins ties. Each pays the dial power selected by deducting it from the Power Track; played cards are discarded face-up, and card values do not cost extra track power.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–4 specify secret simultaneous selection, abilities, reveal/tie, and payment.

answers.answer: All losing characters, mechs, and workers retreat to their own home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy may instead retreat eligible units and carried workers to adjacent lakes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat (including workers carried by defeated lake mechs); a winning defender loses none, subject to Polania Camaraderie's stated exception. A non-Saxony winner places a combat star if they have zero or one combat stars, and none if they already have two; Saxony must place one after every victory while it has star tokens. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 5–6 specify retreats/resources, popularity, star limits, and losing-player card reward.

answers.answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter if the character remains there. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the token stays. Gains of resources, workers, mechs, and structures go on the encounter territory where the character is. Pay the card's printed cost, but no additional normal action costs or mat benefits, including ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Encounters: after movement and all combats; token stays if contested entry lost; gains on encounter territory; no additional normal action costs or benefits.

answers.answer: Each player's character, on that player's first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning combat if needed), looks at the available cards, chooses one, and returns the rest. Every player can get one; later visits cannot exchange it. The card is a fifth action section with optional top then bottom and the usual no-repeat rule (Rusviet exception). Factory actions grant no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses, or ongoing recruit bonuses. Factory bottom Move moves one unit up to two territories during that action, or a character/mech with Speed up to three; Mine access and normal movement/stop restrictions still apply.
answers.evidence: Factory section gives card timing, one-per-player/no exchange, action rules, and bottom Move distances.

answers.answer: Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, reveal a completed objective; all requirements must be met at that moment, though you may wait to reveal. Place the objective star and put both objective cards on the bottom of their deck. Normally only one objective star; Saxony retains the other card after the first and can score both.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements paragraph.

answers.answer: Stars are earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on the board, one revealed completed objective, a combat victory (up to two stars), 18 popularity, or 16 power. A star is permanent even if power or popularity later drops; other players' stars do not block a goal. The sixth star ends play immediately, with no equalizing turns or further actions.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end paragraph.

answers.answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, collect its primary benefit, coins, and your ongoing recruit benefit before placing that star. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that part of movement and return initiating units to where they came from; do not resolve another combat. For neighbor power/popularity recruit stars, finish the active action, then resolve active player first, left neighbor second, right neighbor third, checking for the sixth star at each step; if an earlier player placed the sixth star, later recruit stars and bonuses do not resolve.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end paragraph gives bottom-action priority, battle undo, and recruit sequence.

answers.answer: At popularity 10, use the 7–12 tier: $4 per star, $3 per territory counted, and $2 per complete pair of controlled resources. Five stars add $20; four normal territories plus a controlled Factory count as 7 territories and add $21; 13 resources make 6 pairs and add $12. Thus these categories add $53 to held coins, before any structure bonus. The selected structure bonus scores from your structures even if enemies control their territories. Tiebreakers: workers + mechs + structures (not character), power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, then stars placed.
answers.evidence: Final fortune tier table; Factory counts three; structure bonus eligibility; tiebreaker order.

answers.answer: A home base is not a territory. By default you cannot move back into any home base; setup and forced retreats are exceptions, as is Crimea's unlocked Wayfare. Two bases without matching core factions are inactive expansion placeholders.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: base not a territory and default entry ban; expansion placeholders inactive.

answers.answer: Mountain produces metal, tundra oil, farm food, forest wood, and village a worker; lake and Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if needed.
answers.evidence: Produce terrain table; resources section says workers are not resources and no supply limit.

answers.answer: All units may pick up, carry, and drop any number of resources during movement; a mech may pick up or drop resources and workers mid-movement, and may carry any number of your workers, never your character. Speed gives each selected character/mech one extra territory of movement, not workers; a tunnel jump costs one step, so the extra step can be before or after it. Stops for enemy units and character encounters override Speed.
answers.evidence: Move section describes carrying; Speed paragraph gives extra step and stop overrides.

answers.answer: Yes. Any unit may enter an enemy-structure-only territory and take control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.
answers.evidence: Move: 'Enemy structure only'; 'All printed tunnel territories are adjacent ... by any unit.'

answers.answer: You may take a dead turn: move the token to a different section and take neither action. You never pay only part of a cost; a Produce cost must be paid in full if taking Produce. Since Move was the last section used, you must choose a different section this turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure says dead turn requires different section and neither action; never pay partial cost.

answers.answer: A built Armory grants one power on Trade; a built Monument grants one popularity on Bolster. They trigger on those matching actions. You retain structure abilities even without control, and enemy units do not gain them; only Mill production is limited to when controlled.
answers.evidence: Bolster, Trade and Control sections state bonuses and control effect.

answers.answer: Each faction's Riverwalk applies to its character and mechs: Rusviet to farms and villages; Crimea to farms and tundra; Nordic to forests and mountains; Polania to villages and mountains; Saxony to forests and mountains. Nordic Swim instead lets workers alone cross rivers to any land terrain, not lakes; it does not help Nordic character or mechs.
answers.evidence: Faction and unlocked mech abilities table: Riverwalk destinations and Nordic Swim description.

answers.answer: Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels, including its Mine, adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and the Factory adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Workers cannot use these shortcuts.
answers.evidence: Other unlocked mech abilities: Underpass and Township entries specify character/mech Move actions.

answers.answer: Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or its Mine and makes the opponent lose two power on the track, once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery instead lets Nordic pay one power before combat to reduce the opponent's power by two, once per combat, not per unit.
answers.evidence: Saxony Underpass/Disarm and Nordic Seaworthy/Artillery descriptions.

answers.answer: Two mechs and three workers can play three cards total: one per participating character/mech plus one additional card total when workers are present under People's Army. Workers alone never fight; a character or mech is still required.
answers.evidence: Rusviet People's Army: one additional card total; example says two mechs and three workers allow three cards; workers alone never fight.

answers.answer: Crimea Wayfare lets character/mechs move from a territory or home base to Crimea's own or any inactive faction home base regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases. It cannot move them into an active opponent's home base.
answers.evidence: Crimea Wayfare entry specifies destinations and excludes active opponent base.

answers.answer: Crimea Scout steals one random opponent combat card into your hand before combat, once per combat, not per unit. Coercion lets Crimea spend one combat card as any one resource regardless of its value, once per turn.
answers.evidence: Crimea Wayfare/Scout and Crimea Coercion descriptions.

answers.answer: Nordic Seaworthy allows character/mechs to move to and from lakes and retreat to an adjacent lake instead of home. Polania Submerge allows character/mechs to move to and from lakes and from any lake to any other lake; Polania has no Nordic-style adjacent-lake retreat exception. With either ability, workers on lakes require a mech to move off, and carried workers or resources cannot be left behind on a lake when their carrier leaves.
answers.evidence: Nordic Seaworthy, Polania Submerge, and lake-carrying paragraph.

answers.answer: Polania Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after Polania wins combat as aggressor on its turn. It does not prevent popularity loss for driving off undefended workers without combat.
answers.evidence: Polania Camaraderie description explicitly states both scope and exclusion.

answers.answer: Polania may choose up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order; the first gain can pay the second option's cost. It may take as little of each selected benefit as desired, while paying the printed costs.
answers.evidence: Polania Meander: up to two different options in either order; first gain can pay second cost. Encounter rules allow taking less benefit.

answers.answer: No. A character entering an encounter-token territory stops and cannot move again that turn, including during Factory Move. Resolve the encounter only after the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains there.
answers.evidence: Move and Encounters sections state encounter stop and after-combats timing; Factory says normal stop restrictions apply.

answers.answer: Combat-card hand count is public, but during combat you may conceal whether you committed any cards until reveal; card contents remain secret until revealed. Objective contents are secret until revealing a completed objective. Coins are not hidden information, but you need not reveal their exact total value when asked.
answers.evidence: Public and hidden information table.

answers.answer: Coins are the only tangible items exchangeable; tournament play forbids even coin exchanges for deals or alliances. Informal agreements are unenforceable. Negotiation or payment cannot cancel combat already initiated by moving units onto opposing units, though bribes may influence the outcome.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements paragraph.

answers.answer: Popularity 0–6: $3 per star, $2 per territory counted, $1 per complete resource pair. Popularity 7–12: $4, $3, and $2 respectively. Popularity 13–18: $5, $4, and $3 respectively. Controlled lakes count; home bases do not. Only complete pairs score, so a leftover single resource scores nothing.
answers.evidence: Final fortune popularity table; controlled lakes count and home bases do not; complete pairs and odd leftover ignored.

answers.answer: For each adjacency tile, count unique qualifying features across all your structures; rivers do not break adjacency. Count printed tunnel territories, not Mines. Count unique printed encounter locations even if the token was removed. Count unique lakes. Payouts for each category are: 1 feature $2; 2–3 $4; 4–5 $6; and tunnels up to 6 pay $9 at 6, encounters up to 6–7 pay $9 at 6–7, lakes up to 6–7 pay $9 at 6–7; the table leaves no payout beyond the stated maximum.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus table: adjacency categories, unique-feature rule, Mines/removed-token treatment, and payouts.

answers.answer: Structures on tunnels counts structures on printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1 pays $2, 2 pays $4, 3–4 pay $6. Structures in a row counts only your longest continuous straight line; rivers do not break it: 1 pays $2, 2 pays $4, 3 pays $6, 4 pays $9. Structures on farms/tundras counts qualifying structures combined: 1 pays $2, 2 pays $4, 3 pays $6, 4 pays $9.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus table lists qualifications and payouts for these three tiles.

answers.answer: Yes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake.
answers.evidence: Combat step 6 explicitly includes workers carried by defeated lake mechs.

answers.answer: No. A placed star is permanent, but current popularity still determines final scoring, so a popularity star does not preserve the current popularity tier. Other players' stars never block a goal, so two factions can both earn stars for the same achievement.
answers.evidence: Stars paragraph: star permanent while current popularity determines scoring; other players' stars never block a goal.

answers.answer: Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Seat factions in board order clockwise: Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania, omitting inactive factions. Immediate left/right neighbors matter because their corresponding bottom-row actions can trigger your ongoing recruit bonuses; in two-player play the opponent triggers once, not twice.
answers.evidence: Setup mat-deal and faction seating steps; Ongoing recruits defines neighbor triggers.

answers.answer: A river is a border between two land territories; a lake occupies an entire hex and extends to every adjacent shoreline. A unit with an applicable lake-movement ability may enter from any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.
answers.evidence: Move: river/lake definitions and lake entry rule.

answers.answer: No, you may not keep a drawn encounter card private: show it to all players, show its artwork, and read the capitalized thematic text aloud. You need not read every option aloud.
answers.evidence: Encounters: show card and artwork; read capitalized thematic text; options need not all be read aloud.

answers.answer: There is no limit to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: 'No limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.'

answers.answer: The next clockwise player may begin their turn after the current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, while the current player decides which upgrade, mech, structure, or recruit to gain.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: next player may begin while current player decides which piece to gain after starting a noninteractive bottom action.

answers.answer: No. You may take the top action at most once and the bottom action at most once within a turn, including Rusviet; repeating the section does not let you repeat either action during that turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: top and bottom actions each limited to once within turn, including Rusviet.

answers.answer: If you choose not to move units, the normal Move action lets you gain $1 instead.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: alternatively gain $1.

answers.answer: No. Workers never return to the Player Mat; even workers that retreat to your home base are not returned to it. Thus an on-board worker cannot be reused to cover a Produce cost.
answers.evidence: Produce: 'Workers never return to the Player Mat'; retreat rules send workers to home base.

answers.answer: Yes. You may attack with zero power, zero popularity, or both.
answers.evidence: Combat: 'You may attack with zero power/popularity.'

answers.answer: Yes. You may still fight after reaching the non-Saxony limit of two combat stars; further wins do not award another combat star.
answers.evidence: Combat step 5: winner with two combat stars places none; 'You may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit.'

answers.answer: A faction without Meander must choose one affordable option and cannot decline to choose. It cannot select unaffordable coin/popularity options. It may take as little of the chosen option's benefit as desired, while paying the printed cost.
answers.evidence: Encounters: must choose one affordable option; cannot decline; unaffordable options unavailable; may take less benefit.

answers.answer: No: combatants select their dials simultaneously and secretly, not in turn order. Dials and any selected cards are revealed simultaneously after both choose.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1 and 3: both secretly choose simultaneously; reveal simultaneously.

answers.answer: Announce the bottom-row action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: 'Announce the action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.'

answers.answer: No. Place a star as soon as you achieve a star goal; the sixth star immediately ends play. A completed objective is different: you may wait to reveal it, but must meet all requirements at the moment you eventually reveal it.
answers.evidence: Stars: place as soon as achieved and sixth star ends immediately; Objectives: may wait to reveal, requirements at reveal.

answers.answer: No. By default, units cannot cross rivers or enter lakes; faction and mech abilities provide exceptions.
answers.evidence: Move: units cannot normally cross rivers or enter lakes; abilities provide exceptions.

answers.answer: No. The recruit is permanently placed on the Faction Mat one-time bonus space and cannot later move.
answers.evidence: Enlist: recruit goes permanently on an open one-time bonus and 'cannot later move.'

answers.answer: No. Only a character triggers an encounter; a mech or worker entering the territory does not resolve it or remove its token.
answers.evidence: Encounters: 'Only a character triggers an encounter.'

answers.answer: While controlled, the Mill provides one bonus production territory in addition to those normally selected: normally up to two becomes up to three; an upgraded allowance of three becomes up to four. The Mill itself counts as one producing worker; actual workers there also produce normally, so their output is added rather than substituted. It can produce without an actual worker there, using the terrain table. If enemy units control the territory, the Mill cannot produce.
answers.evidence: Produce: Mill paragraph specifies bonus territory, worker/output behavior, empty Mill, and control requirement.

answers.answer: You control a territory if you have a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. Resources alone do not establish control; after your last unit leaves a territory with no structure, you no longer control it just because resources remain.
answers.evidence: Control definition: unit or structure with no enemy unit; resources do not appear as a control condition.

answers.answer: Build is paid with wood; Enlist is paid with food.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row resources: 'Upgrade oil; Deploy metal; Build wood; Enlist food.'
